definition: The exact string format that wraps a conversation (system/user/assistant turns, special tokens) before tokenization.
details: The exact string format that wraps a conversation (system/user/assistant turns, special tokens) before tokenization. Every model family has its own; applying the wrong template is one of the most common causes of degraded fine-tuned or self-hosted model behavior.

explainer.lead: A chat template turns conversation turns into the exact text a model expects before that text is tokenized. Using the right one matters because even correct messages can produce poor behavior when their roles and special tokens are formatted incorrectly.

tiers.eli5: Imagine putting each speaker's lines into a script with special labels showing who is talking. A chat template is the rule for making that script, so the model can tell instructions, questions, and answers apart. A different model may need a different script layout.
tiers.practitioner: Apply the template belonging to the model family when preparing fine-tuning conversations and when serving the resulting model. Check the fully rendered string, including role markers, special tokens, and turn boundaries, before tokenization; a mismatch between training and inference templates can degrade behavior.
tiers.paperLevel: Let a conversation C consist of ordered turns (r_i, m_i), where r_i is a role such as system, user, or assistant and m_i is its text. A chat template is a deterministic formatting function T(C) = s, followed by tokenization Tokenize(s) = x; T is model-family-specific, and no universal template is implied.

explainer.example: For the turns system: "Be brief.", user: "Hi", and assistant: "Hello!", an illustrative template might render "<system>Be brief.</system><user>Hi</user><assistant>Hello!</assistant>". That exact string, including its markers, is then tokenized; another model family may require different markers or spacing.

usedIn.name: Supervised fine-tuning
usedIn.detail: Formats system, user, and assistant turns consistently throughout the training conversations.

usedIn.name: Self-hosted chat inference
usedIn.detail: Renders incoming messages with the model family's expected roles and special tokens.

usedIn.name: Conversation dataset preparation
usedIn.detail: Converts structured message records into strings ready for tokenization.

explainer.intuition: A model receives tokens, not a messaging app's neatly separated speech bubbles. The chat template is the convention that encodes those bubbles, their speakers, and their boundaries as one precise string.
howItWorks: Start with ordered system, user, and assistant turns.
Select the template associated with the target model family.
Insert role markers, message text, special tokens, and turn boundaries exactly as that template specifies.
Pass the resulting single string to the tokenizer.
Use the same formatting convention during fine-tuning and subsequent inference.
explainer.whyItMatters: The template preserves the conversation structure the model expects to see. Applying the wrong model family's template is a common cause of degraded behavior in fine-tuned or self-hosted models.
misconceptions: A chat template is not tokenization: it produces the string that tokenization then consumes.
Templates are not interchangeable across model families, even when they represent the same roles.
